items.title: 68426_Nellie Lutcher oral history interview
items.q: for a little while I studied under Mrs. Foster

ctx.x: She egged me on and encouraged me on, and she showed me all the -- whatever she could. I shall never forget one time at a graduation exercise, she had me to play the 'Blue Danube Waltz' behind a choral group. Yes, and I was very young

at the time, very small, and this was so marvelous, because at the time we had a woman in Lake Charles who was -- I can't remember her maiden name, but her name was Mrs. Alton J. Foster, who was also a very magnificent concert pianist. Her husband at one time I think was the President of the rice mill up there, if I'm not mistaken. And she happened to have been at this particular event and she was very inspired by me, and she contacted my teacher and she told her she would like her to bring me down to her home,…

But anyway, Mrs. Eugenia Reynaud was also the organist and the pianist of the little Baptist Church where we belonged, the Sunlight Baptist Church in Lake Charles. And she trained me to be her assistant at the church, and then I used to play for her at Sunday school. I became the Sunday school pianist. I was getting the big sum of $2.00 a month.
